publishedRecipe.name: Southwest Salmon Chowder with Potato, Corn, Bell Pepper & Avocado

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 medium yellow potatoes
2 red bell peppers
1 lime
1 avocado

instructions.primary_message: Peel and small dice potatoes; place in a medium bowl.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell peppers; add to the bowl with the potato and set aside.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
While the pot heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add potato, bell pepper, and onion; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 3-4 minutes.
Sprinkle flour and spices over the veggies; continue to cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 tsp chili powder
1 tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add broth and milk to the pot, stir to combine, and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat to medium, and cook until potatoes are tender, 10-12 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
48 fl oz (6 cups) chicken or vegetable broth
16 fl oz (2 cups) whole milk

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, slice lime into wedges and set aside for serving.
Halve and pit avocado; slice crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out with a spoon.
When the soup is done, drain and break salmon into chunks; add to the pot, along with the corn, and stir to combine. Cook until heated through, 3-4 minutes more. Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 (7.5 oz) cans wild pink salmon, traditional style
1 ⅓ cups frozen corn

instructions.primary_message: Divide soup between bowls, top with avocado, and sprinkle with additional chili powder. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing and enjoy!
